overview: Lam Research is a global supplier of wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) and related services to the semiconductor industry, specializing in deposition, etch, and clean process technologies used to build memory, foundry, and logic/IDM chips. Products range from leading-edge systems (ALTUS, SABRE, VECTOR, Kiyo, Flex, Akara, Vantex, Aether dry-EUV-resist) to the Customer Support Business Group (CSBG), which services, upgrades, and sells refurbished/non-leading-edge equipment (Reliant line) across an installed base deployed through facilities and service networks in the U.S., China, Europe, India, Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia, and Taiwan. Fiscal 2026 (ended June 28, 2026) revenue was $23.2 billion, up 26% YoY, with non-U.S. sales consistently ~92-93% of revenue and China alone representing 34-35% of revenue in FY2026 and the September 2026 quarter.

business_model.summary: Lam sells capital equipment (systems) for new fab capacity/technology transitions plus a growing, stickier Customer Support Business Group (CSBG) tied to the installed base (spares, service, upgrades, Reliant refurbished tools). Systems revenue is lumpy and transactional/project-based, driven by customer capex cycles; CSBG revenue is more recurring and grows with the installed base regardless of new-tool spending, acting as a partial cyclical buffer. FY2026: Systems revenue $14.9B (64% of total, +29.5% YoY) vs. Customer support-related revenue and other $8.35B (36%, +20.2% YoY). By end market (% of leading/non-leading-edge equipment and upgrade revenue), FY2026: Foundry 54% (up from 45% in FY2025, driven by mature-node and leading-edge investment), Memory 39% (down from 42%), Logic/IDM 7% (down from 13%). In the September 2026 quarter (Q1 FY2027), Foundry and Memory each represented 46% of revenue and Logic/IDM 8%, with memory growing faster in absolute dollars as AI/HBM-driven DRAM spending accelerated.

revenue_streams.name: Customer support-related revenue and other (service, spares, upgrades, Reliant)

business_model.customer_type: B2B: concentrated base of the world's largest semiconductor memory, foundry, and IDM manufacturers; most significant customers across FY2024-FY2026 were Micron, Samsung, SK hynix, and TSMC
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2026 revenue by customer-facility location: China 34%, Taiwan 22%, Korea 19%, Japan 9%, United States 7%, Southeast Asia 6%, Europe 3%. Q1 FY2027 (Sept 2026 quarter): China 35%, Korea 20%, Taiwan 18%, Japan 9%, US 8%, SE Asia 6%, Europe 4%. Non-U.S. sales were ~92-93% of revenue in FY2026, FY2025, and the September 2026 quarter.

main_competitors: Chinese domestic toolmakers (e.g., AMEC, Naura, Piotech) gaining share amid export controls
competitive_position.market_position: Leading pure-play in etch and a top-tier player in deposition and clean; estimated overall WFE market share has been rising (third-party estimates put Lam around 11-13% of total WFE in 2025-2026, versus Applied Materials in the high-teens/high-single-to-20% range, Tokyo Electron low-teens, and KLA ~8%, though vendor estimates vary). Lam states it believes it holds a strong competitive position in deposition, etch, and clean, with particular strength in high-aspect-ratio etch for 3D NAND and DRAM scaling.

moat_factors.description: Once a semiconductor manufacturer qualifies a supplier's equipment for a specific production application and technology node, it typically continues purchasing that supplier's tools for that application for an extended period -- the company's own 10-K flags this as a two-sided risk (hard to win a customer who qualified a competitor, but sticky once Lam is qualified)

Large global installed base feeds proprietary process data back into R&D ('cycles of learning'), reinforcing product performance advantages and supporting a growing, higher-margin CSBG service/spares/upgrade revenue stream

moat_factors.factor: Technology leadership in etch/deposition for advanced scaling
moat_factors.description: Differentiated high-aspect-ratio etch, ALD/CVD metallization, and new dry-EUV-resist (Aether) technologies positioned for gate-all-around logic, advanced 3D NAND, and HBM/advanced-packaging transitions

Significant, sustained R&D investment (~10% of revenue) across a broad deposition/etch/clean product portfolio supports technology-inflection capture, though Lam itself notes its narrower product-line focus versus larger diversified competitors is also a risk
Deep co-development relationships with leading memory/foundry/logic customers (Micron, Samsung, SK hynix, TSMC) embed Lam early in next-generation process development

weaknesses: High customer concentration: a handful of large customers (Micron, Samsung, SK hynix, TSMC) drive a significant share of revenue, cash flow, and receivables; any one customer's capex pullback or payment issue is disproportionately impactful
Narrower product-line diversification than larger competitors (e.g., Applied Materials) that offer more comprehensive multi-step solutions, which the company itself flags as a competitive weakness

Heavy, concentrated China revenue exposure (34-35% of revenue) now under direct pressure from expanding U.S. export controls, entity listings, and case-specific shipment halts (e.g., Hua Hong in April 2026), with Chinese customers increasingly substituting domestic toolmakers
Extreme revenue/order variability tied to a small number of high-dollar-value systems (tens of millions per system), so losing even a few deals can materially swing quarterly results
Reliance on single or limited-source suppliers for certain components, with exposure to rare-earth-element export controls from China

growth_drivers: AI-driven wafer fab equipment (WFE) supercycle: management has raised its calendar 2026 WFE market estimate to the low/mid-$150 billion range and given a preliminary calendar 2027 outlook above $200 billion, with DRAM (led by HBM) expected to drive the largest incremental growth, followed by leading-edge foundry/logic and then NAND

HBM production requires substantially more deposition/etch/clean process steps per wafer than conventional memory, directly increasing Lam's addressable content per wafer as HBM capacity scales for AI accelerators

Gate-all-around/nanosheet logic transitions, advanced 3D NAND scaling, and advanced packaging (including fan-out panel-level packaging and 3D HBM stacking via SABRE 3D) expand served available market in deposition and etch
Dry EUV photoresist (Aether) and Numerical Aperture EUV-enabled patterning create a new, differentiated product category tied to next-generation lithography adoption
Growing, higher-margin, more resilient Customer Support Business Group (CSBG) revenue as the global installed base expands, buffering cyclicality in systems revenue

Capital return program: $25 billion new share repurchase authorization and a raised quarterly dividend ($0.33, announced November 5, 2026) signal confidence in sustained free cash flow, with a stated goal of returning a majority of free cash flow to shareholders over time
Geographic diversification of fab investment (U.S., Taiwan, Korea CHIPS-Act- and AI-driven capacity buildouts) partially offsetting China-specific headwinds

business.description: Revenue, cash flow, and accounts receivable are concentrated among a small number of large customers (Micron, Samsung, SK hynix, TSMC); as of June 28, 2026 five customers represented approximately 20%, 16%, 15%, 11%, and 10% of accounts receivable

WFE demand has historically swung sharply with memory pricing, IC demand, and macro conditions; a slower-than-expected AI adoption curve, compute-efficiency gains, or an AI-infrastructure oversupply could sharply reduce customer capex

A substantial percentage of revenue comes from a limited number of high-dollar-value systems; losing even a few large orders can materially swing quarterly revenue, and tool-qualification dynamics make it hard to win share from an installed competitor

U.S. export controls have pushed some former Chinese customers toward domestic equipment suppliers (e.g., AMEC, Naura), and new-customer additions in China have slowed, per management commentary at industry conferences in early 2026

financial.description: Revenue is mostly USD-denominated, but Japanese yen revenue and euro/Korean won/Malaysian ringgit/Indian rupee-denominated expenses create hedged and unhedged FX exposure

Effective tax rate rose to 12.1% in FY2026 from 10.1% in FY2025 (GMT/BEPS 2.0 effectiveness) and to 16.9% in the September 2026 quarter; a 15-year Malaysia tax incentive (benefiting diluted EPS by ~$0.77 in FY2026) is a disclosed, time-limited tailwind
The majority of cash is generated outside the U.S., constraining onshore liquidity available for buybacks/dividends/debt service without repatriation or financing

regulatory.description: China represented 34%, 34%, and 42% of total revenue in FY2026, FY2025, and FY2024, respectively; expanding U.S. Entity List additions, foreign direct product rule changes tied to Huawei, and case-specific actions (e.g., an April 2026 'is-informed' letter halting certain tool shipments to Hua Hong/Huali) have already reduced and could further reduce China revenue and open the door to foreign (non-U.S.) competitors not subject to the same restrictions

regulatory.risk: Chinese retaliatory export controls on rare earth elements
regulatory.description: China has imposed export controls/license requirements on certain rare earth elements and on products made outside China containing Chinese-origin rare earths (partially suspended until November 2026 absent extension), which could delay or increase the cost of Lam's own manufacturing inputs

regulatory.risk: Tariffs on steel/aluminum and other inputs
regulatory.description: FY2026 steel and aluminum tariffs on U.S. imports increased manufacturing costs and adversely affected margins; broader tariff/trade-barrier escalation is an ongoing disclosed risk
Proposed regulations could require transitioning away from PFAS-containing materials used in products and supply chain, with no assurance of cost-equivalent substitutes

macro.risk: Geopolitical instability affecting supply chains and commodities
macro.description: The 2026 Middle East conflict (US/Israel/Gulf states/Iran) disrupted oil, LNG, and industrial commodities (aluminum, helium, bromine, sulfur) important to the semiconductor industry, with potential to magnify other risks

macro.risk: Interest rate and credit market sensitivity
macro.description: Customer capex decisions are sensitive to the cost and availability of capital; tightening global credit conditions could delay or reduce fab investment

Lam's growth outlook (2027 WFE >$200B) is highly levered to continued hyperscaler/memory-maker AI infrastructure investment; any broad AI capex pause or correction would flow directly through to WFE orders

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Management has raised its calendar 2026 WFE market estimate into the low-to-mid $150 billion range (from an earlier ~$140 billion) and given a preliminary calendar 2027 outlook of more than $200 billion, with DRAM (driven by HBM for AI accelerators) expected to lead growth, followed by leading-edge foundry/logic, then NAND.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Historically highly cyclical, tracking semiconductor manufacturers' capital expenditure cycles; the current AI/HBM-driven investment wave has extended and amplified the up-cycle, but management and risk disclosures both flag that a slowdown in AI adoption, an efficiency breakthrough, or compute oversupply could sharply reverse demand
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect but meaningful: customer fab investment decisions are sensitive to the cost and availability of capital; Lam itself carries $3.75 billion of fixed-rate long-term debt (fair value $3.16 billion as of June 28, 2026) whose market value (not cash flows) is interest-rate sensitive
key_input_costs: Rare earth elements and related materials (subject to Chinese export controls)
Semiconductor components used in Lam's own tools

recent_developments.event: Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.33/share (up from $0.26) and authorized an additional $25 billion share repurchase program

Reported Q1 FY2027 (September 2026 quarter) results: revenue $8.22 billion (+54% YoY, +22% QoQ), non-GAAP EPS $2.20, gross margin 52.3%, net income $2.75 billion, diluted GAAP EPS $2.19 -- above the high end of July guidance -- but the stock sold off on concerns the December-quarter (Q2 FY2027) guidance (~$8.6B revenue; ~52.5% gross margin; non-GAAP EPS around $2.33, slightly below some consensus estimates) implied decelerating sequential growth
Management reiterated a bullish preliminary calendar 2027 WFE outlook above $200 billion, calling the setup 'extraordinary,' with DRAM/HBM as the primary growth driver

U.S. Commerce Department reportedly sent 'is-informed' letters to Lam, Applied Materials, and KLA ordering a halt to certain chip-tool shipments to Hua Hong (China's No. 2 foundry) and Huali, adding fresh uncertainty to China revenue

At the UBS Global Technology and AI Conference, management said recent Entity List additions had affected former Chinese customers, pushed demand toward domestic Chinese toolmakers, and slowed the pace of new China customer additions; guided China revenue toward below 30% of total in calendar 2026, down from roughly 34-35%

Filed FY2026 Form 10-K: full-year revenue $23.23 billion (+26.0% YoY), gross margin 50.5% (+180 bps), net income $7.27 billion (+35.6%), diluted EPS $5.76; Systems revenue +29.5% YoY driven by foundry spending, CSBG revenue +20.2%
$750 million of 2026 Senior Notes matured and were settled with cash on hand; commercial paper program capacity increased from $1.50 billion to $2.00 billion

items.notes: Implies continued sequential growth off Q1 FY2027's $8.22 billion, though growth rate decelerating from the September quarter's 22% QoQ increase; some coverage cites the figure as slightly below the high end of Street expectations, triggering a post-earnings share-price decline
Up modestly from Q1 FY2027's 52.3% actual

items.target: ~$2.33 (some sources cite a range around $2.00-2.30 lower bound debate)
items.notes: Slightly below some sell-side consensus (~$2.34), partly attributed to a higher expected tax rate; secondary sources disagree on the exact point estimate, so treat as approximate pending the company's own release/transcript
Raised from an earlier ~$140 billion estimate; AI demand cited as driving higher spending across both memory and non-memory segments
Preliminary outlook; DRAM (led by HBM) expected to drive the largest growth, followed by leading-edge foundry/logic, then NAND

items.vs_prior: lowered (as % of mix, reflecting export-control impact)
items.notes: Down from roughly 34-35% in FY2025/FY2026; management expects AI-driven capacity buildouts in the U.S., Taiwan, and Korea to offset a meaningful portion of the China revenue decline over time

items.target: $25 billion new buyback authorization; quarterly dividend raised to $0.33/share
items.notes: Dividend payable January 6, 2027 to holders of record December 2, 2026; repurchase program has no termination date

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Tim Archer and CFO Doug Bettinger framed the September 2026 quarter as a record driven by strong foundry and memory equipment demand, with memory (DRAM/HBM) overtaking foundry as a growth driver on an absolute-dollar basis. Management described the preliminary calendar 2027 WFE setup (>$200 billion) as 'extraordinary,' tied to AI-driven HBM and leading-edge capacity investment, while flagging that December-quarter guidance implies a deceleration in sequential growth versus the September quarter's pace. Management continues to guide China's revenue share down (toward below 30% in 2026) given export-control pressure, while expressing confidence that AI-related capacity buildouts in the U.S., Taiwan, and Korea will offset a majority of that decline over time.

bull_case: AI/HBM-driven memory investment supercycle: management's calendar 2027 WFE outlook of >$200 billion, if realized, implies a multi-year step-up in Lam's addressable market, since HBM production requires substantially more deposition/etch/clean steps per wafer than conventional memory
Record FY2026 results (revenue +26%, net income +36%, gross margin +180bps) demonstrate operating leverage and favorable customer/product mix as foundry and memory spending both recover
Diversification of fab investment toward the U.S., Taiwan, and Korea provides a structural offset to China-specific export-control headwinds, reducing single-region dependence over time

Strong balance sheet and free cash flow generation support an aggressive capital return program ($25 billion new buyback authorization, dividend raised to $0.33/quarter), signaling management confidence
Technology leadership in etch and advanced deposition positions Lam to capture share in gate-all-around logic, advanced 3D NAND, and next-generation EUV patterning (Aether dry resist) transitions
bear_case: China export-control escalation (Entity List expansions, Hua Hong-style shipment halts, foreign direct product rule changes) is actively eroding a historically ~34-42%-of-revenue market, with limited near-term offset and the risk that non-U.S. competitors (Tokyo Electron, and increasingly local Chinese toolmakers) capture share Lam cannot contest

Q2 FY2027 guidance, while raised in absolute terms, implied a deceleration in sequential growth and triggered a sharp post-earnings share-price decline (several-percent drop reported), suggesting the market is pricing in flawless execution against very high AI-capex expectations

Heavy customer concentration (Micron, Samsung, SK hynix, TSMC) means a pullback or delay by even one large customer could materially swing results; the AI-capex cycle itself is a bet on hyperscaler/memory-maker spending staying elevated

Highly cyclical, big-ticket systems revenue model means Lam's results can swing sharply if AI infrastructure spending decelerates, compute-efficiency gains reduce chip demand, or memory pricing/supply dynamics shift

Elevated reliance on a Malaysia tax incentive (benefiting FY2026 diluted EPS by ~$0.77) and rising effective tax rates (12.1% FY2026, 16.9% in the September 2026 quarter) create underappreciated downside risk to reported EPS growth
